summary: Google DeepMind introduced SL2T, a new sign-language-to-text translation model, and launched it as a sign-to-text dictation feature in Gboard and Live Transcribe on Pixel 11, starting with American Sign Language to English.

practices.reason: SL2T is a new model that translates streaming body/hand pose sequences into text with a stated benchmark result, but the domain is narrow (sign language) and not something most engineering teams build on directly.
practices.quote: SL2T achieves a remarkable zero-shot score of 70 BLEURT, which is significantly higher than any previously reported score.

practices.reason: The team describes benchmark methodology (FLEURS-ASL, BLEURT) and practical eval concerns like hallucination on non-signing input and fairness across left- and one-handed signers, useful measurement practice but tied to the lab's own internal process.
practices.quote: SL2T is the most capable sign language translation model to date according to key benchmarks like FLEURS-ASL (sd-test), which assesses ASL to English translation quality.
